notes: New: choose the battery in the flight planner: Standard (2590 mAh) or Plus (3850 mAh). The battery estimate then learns only from your flights with that battery, so a Plus-battery plan isn't judged by standard-battery flights (and the other way round)
The map tells the two batteries apart by itself: every flight log records the battery's size. Open a flight to see which one it used ("Battery pack")
Haven't flown one of them yet? The estimate is worked out from your flights with the other one and DJI's flight times (34 min standard, 45 min Plus)
With the Plus battery the drone weighs more than 249 g: the planner reminds you that the rules for heavier drones apply (in the US: FAA registration and Remote ID)
New plans start with the battery of your most recent flight
Point at a place's icon on the map to see its name and what kind of place it is, even when you're zoomed out and the names are hidden
The plan flags in the Plans tab stand out much more: bigger, brighter, with a pulsing ring (it stays still if your computer is set to reduce motion)

Places: when Azure's places can't be used (today's searches used up, or Azure didn't answer), the layers panel now says why, and that OpenStreetMap's places are shown instead. After a one-off hiccup Azure is asked again 5 minutes later (it used to stay on OpenStreetMap until the page was reloaded). The "Places come from" line now names the right company
